metas.name: Grave of the Fireflies
metas.description:
Captures war as two children slowly running out of everything. A brother tries to keep his little sister fed and cheerful in Kobe, 1945, making worse decisions out of pride.

A young boy and his little sister struggle to survive in Japan during World War II.

metas.name: Perfect Blue
metas.description:
Captures fame eating a person's grip on which self is hers. A pop idol turned actress, a stalker, and a fan site narrating her life in first person — the animated form is what makes the slippage work.

A pop singer gives up her career to become an actress, but she slowly goes insane when she starts being stalked by an obsessed fan and what seems to be a ghost of her past.

metas.name: Waltz with Bashir
metas.description:
Captures a soldier's memory with a hole in it. Animated interviews as the director tries to recover what he did in Beirut in 1982, ending with footage that breaks the animation open.

An Israeli film director interviews fellow veterans of the 1982 invasion of Lebanon to reconstruct his own memories of his term of service in that conflict.

metas.name: Flee
metas.description:
Captures telling a hidden life story for the first time. An animated documentary about a refugee from Afghanistan settled in Denmark, recounting flight, family separation and a secret he has kept from everyone.

A man looks back over his life as he grapples with a painful secret he has kept hidden for 20 years, one that threatens to derail the life he has built for himself and his soon to be husband.

metas.name: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse
metas.director: Bob Persichetti, Peter Ramsey, Rodney Rothman
metas.description:
Captures what a comic book actually feels like to read, in motion. Also a genuinely good story about a kid learning that anyone can wear the mask, by failing at it a lot.

Teen Miles Morales becomes the Spider-Man of his universe and must join with five spider-powered individuals from other dimensions to stop a threat for all realities.

metas.name: Princess Mononoke
metas.description:
Captures an ecological war with no pure side. Iron Town needs the forest cut to survive; the forest gods need the humans gone; a prince cursed by a dying god tries to see with unclouded eyes.

After a deadly curse forces him from home, young warrior Ashitaka journeys west and is drawn into a conflict between ancient forest spirits, an iron town, and a wolf-raised girl.

metas.name: Paddington 2
metas.description:
Captures decency as something contagious. A bear framed for stealing the pop-up book he wanted to buy his aunt, sent to prison — and the prison improves because he is in it.

Paddington, now happily settled with the Brown family and a popular member of the local community, picks up a series of odd jobs to buy the perfect present for his Aunt Lucy's 100th birthday, only for the gift to be stolen.

metas.name: Paprika
metas.description:
Captures dreams invading waking life as a parade. A device that lets therapists enter dreams is stolen, and reality dissolves into a marching band of refrigerators and dolls; Inception's debt is on screen.

When a machine that allows therapists to enter their patients' dreams is stolen, all hell breaks loose. Only a young female therapist, Paprika, can stop it.

metas.name: It's Such a Beautiful Day
metas.description:
Captures a mind coming apart, drawn with stick figures. Hertzfeldt narrates a man with a failing brain in three chapters — funny, fragmented, and by the end genuinely cosmic.

Bill struggles to put together his shattered psyche, in this new feature film version of Don Hertzfeldt's animated short film trilogy.

metas.name: The Tale of the Princess Kaguya
metas.description:
Captures joy being disciplined out of a girl. A bamboo cutter raises a moon princess and watches court life sand down the wild child she was, until the watercolour lines themselves start to run.

Kaguya is a beautiful young woman coveted by five nobles. To try to avoid marrying a stranger she doesn't love, she sends her suitors on seemingly impossible tasks. But she will have to face her fate and punishment for her choices.

metas.name: Wolfwalkers
metas.description:
Captures the wild being hunted in the name of order. Kilkenny, 1650: a hunter's daughter befriends a girl who becomes a wolf in her sleep, and Cartoon Saloon's hand-drawn forest keeps breaking out of the town's straight lines.

A young apprentice hunter and her father journey to Ireland to help wipe out the last wolf pack. But everything changes when she befriends a free-spirited girl from a mysterious tribe rumored to transform into wolves by night.

metas.name: Tower
metas.description:
Captures how people inside an event remember it — partial, sensory, nothing like the news summary. The 1966 UT Austin sniper massacre retold in rotoscoped animation from survivors' memories, switching to real footage only at the end.

Animation, testimony, and archival footage combine to relate the events of August 1, 1966 when a gunman opened fire from the University of Texas clock tower, killing 16 people.

metas.name: Tale of Tales
metas.description:
Captures folk memory itself — images from childhood, war and lullaby sharing one continuous dream. Norstein's 29-minute animation drifts through layers of cut-out, glass and mist: a little wolf, a minotaur, tango dancers, soldiers leaving for the front.

Distant, well-worn memories of childhood are inhabited by a little gray wolf. Through astonishing imagery, the memory of all of Russia is depicted.

metas.name: Alice
metas.description:
Captures the folk tale as a child's-eye inventory of a household's dangerous things. Švankmajer's Alice moves through a Wonderland of taxidermy, bones and jam jars of pins, stop-motion objects that genuinely threaten her — Carroll's dream rebuilt from junk drawers.

A surrealistic revision of Alice in Wonderland.

metas.name: Song of the Sea
metas.description:
Captures a selkie myth drawn the way the sea draws on rock. A mute little girl is the last seal-child; her brother resents her for their mother's death, and the rescue journey is rendered in spirals, knots and watercolour geometry from the studio behind The Secret of Kells lineage.

Ben, a young Irish boy and his little sister, Saoirse, a girl who can turn into a seal, go on an adventure to free the fairies and save the spirit world.

metas.name: Ernest & Celestine
metas.director: Stéphane Aubier, Vincent Patar, Benjamin Renner
metas.description:
Captures a bear and a mouse outlawed by both their societies for the friendship. Bears live above, mice below, each raised on horror stories about the other; a watercolor heist and a double trial later, the film has made its whole case with a pencil line and a piano.

The story of an unlikely friendship between a bear, Ernest, and a young mouse named Celestine.

metas.name: Robot Dreams
metas.description:
Captures a friendship conducted entirely without dialogue, in 1980s New York, between a dog and a mail-order robot. They dance to Earth, Wind & Fire on roller skates; a beach closing separates them; the film then does the bravest thing a family film can do with its ending. Wordless, and it earns tears honestly.

The adventures and misfortunes of Dog and Robot in New York City during the 1980s.

metas.name: Flow
metas.description:
Captures animals cooperating after the humans vanish, with no speech and no villain. A cat that fears water survives a flood aboard a drifting boat shared with a capybara, a lemur, a secretary bird and a dog; made in Blender by a tiny Latvian team, and the water alone justifies it.

Cat is a solitary animal, but as its home is devastated by a great flood, he finds refuge on a boat populated by various species, and will have to team up with them despite their differences.

metas.name: Marcel the Shell with Shoes On
metas.description:
Captures an inch-high shell with a breadcrumb for a hat, processing fame and loss at full sincerity. A documentarian films his tiny Airbnb cohabitant, whose missing community and ill grandmother turn stop-motion cuteness into something quietly devastating about scale and care.

A cash-strapped documentary maker decides to make his newest documentary about a mollusk shell he finds living in his Airbnb with his friends.

metas.name: The Adventures of Prince Achmed
metas.description:
Captures the Arabian Nights in cut-paper silhouettes, made frame by frame over three years. The oldest animated feature that survives, and it still moves like a shadow-play dream — flying horses, shape-shifting battles, a witch duel in mid-air.

A handsome prince rides a flying horse to faraway lands and embarks on magical adventures, which include befriending a witch, meeting Aladdin, battling demons and falling in love with a princess.

metas.name: Son of the White Mare
metas.description:
Captures a Hungarian folk tale as a full psychedelic cosmology. A hero raised by a white mare descends to the underworld to free three princesses; every frame is saturated folk-art geometry, trees become faces, cities become breasts, colours carry the mythology. The Parajanov lane, in animation.

In this dreamlike Hungarian folk myth, a horse goddess gives birth to three powerful brothers who set out into the Underworld to save three princesses from three evil dragons and reclaim their ancestors' lost kingdom.

metas.name: Sita Sings the Blues
metas.description:
Captures the Ramayana told four ways at once: 1920s blues vocals by Annette Hanshaw, shadow-puppet narrators bickering over the plot, lush vector animation, and the director's own breakup drawn in squiggles — the same story projected through four transducers, and they don't agree.

An animated version of the epic Indian tale of Ramayana set to the 1920s jazz vocals of Annette Hanshaw.

metas.name: Night on the Galactic Railroad
metas.description:
Captures two cat schoolboys riding a train through the Milky Way, visiting the dead. Kenji Miyazawa's novel rendered in slow, starlit melancholy; the stops along the line are all the ways people leave. The quietest cosmology in this batch.

Two kittens go on a metaphysical journey on a magical railroad train.

metas.name: Angel's Egg
metas.description:
Captures a girl carrying an egg she will not explain, through a drowned Gothic city, followed by a man carrying a cross-shaped weapon. Almost no dialogue; rain, fossils, water tanks full of shadow fish. Oshii lost his faith and made this instead of a sermon.

A mysterious young girl wanders a desolate, otherworldly landscape, carrying a large egg.

metas.name: Belladonna of Sadness
metas.description:
Captures a medieval witch's rise and destruction in watercolours that keep dissolving. A peasant woman bargains with the Devil across still paintings that pan, bleed and occasionally erupt into full animation and psychedelic rock. Suppressed for decades, restored now — maximalism on paper.

After being raped by an evil feudal lord and subsequently getting banished from her village, a peasant girl makes a pact with the Devil to gain magical powers and take her revenge.

metas.name: Millennium Actress
metas.description:
Captures a retired actress's memories edited as the films she starred in. Two documentary makers interview her, and each recollection deposits them inside the scene — feudal Japan, wartime, a space launch — while her one lost love stays a frame ahead. Your projection framework as a life story: the observed biography keeps re-rendering the hidden one.

A TV interviewer and his cameraman meet a former actress and travel through her memories and career.

metas.name: Ghost in the Shell
metas.description:
Captures a cyborg major hunting a hacker who may be the first digital life-form, in long rain-slick silences between the action. The gap in your collection: the film that made "what counts as a self when every layer is replaceable" into mainstream science fiction, and it argues by canal boat and museum tree as much as by dialogue.

A cyborg policewoman and her partner hunt a mysterious and powerful hacker called the Puppet Master.

metas.name: Ghost in the Shell 2: Innocence
metas.description:
Captures a detective and his mostly-robotic partner investigating murdered dolls that begged to die. Denser and stranger than the first: every character quotes philosophy at each other while the camera orbits ball-jointed gynoids in a festival parade that took a year to animate. The observed/observable problem, with dolls as the transducers.

In the year 2032, Batô, a cyborg detective for the anti-terrorist unit Public Security Section 9, investigates the case of a female robot--one created solely for sexual pleasure--who slaughtered her owner.

metas.name: Mind Game
metas.description:
Captures a failed manga artist dying, telling God off, and clawing back to life at maximum velocity. The style mutates per scene — rotoscope, crayon, photo-collage — and the finale is a many-minute sprint through every life he hasn't lived yet. The anti-grit entry: pure forward motion.

After a deadly encounter with two yakuza, a loser with a crush on his childhood girlfriend goes to heaven and back, embarking on a psychedelic self-discovery experience with her and his friends.

metas.name: Redline
metas.description:
Captures the most dangerous race in the galaxy, drawn by hand over seven years. A pompadoured driver, a fascist robot planet, cars that deform like taffy at speed; there is no CGI sheen anywhere, just 100,000 drawings insisting that velocity is a drawing problem.

A story about the most popular racing event in the galaxy, the Redline, and the various racers who compete in it.

metas.name: Inu-Oh
metas.description:
Captures a cursed, contorted Heian-era dancer and a blind biwa player inventing rock concerts in 14th-century Kyoto. Their retellings of the Tales of the Heike make the dead visible to the crowd — and to Inu-Oh himself, whose body straightens as the buried stories get heard. Music as the instrument that reveals the hidden layer; made for you.

A cursed dancer and a musician stun society with electrifying concerts in this animated rock opera.

metas.name: Only Yesterday
metas.description:
Captures a 27-year-old office worker travelling with her 10-year-old self as a permanent passenger. Taeko takes a farm holiday; every adult decision gets cross-examined by the child who wanted fractions explained and a boy to glance at her. Two ages of one person, observing each other, neither in charge.

A twenty-seven-year-old office worker travels to the countryside while reminiscing about her childhood in Tokyo.

metas.name: The Boy and the Heron
metas.description:
Captures a boy following a grey heron into a tower where time pools and the dead curate worlds. Miyazaki's most autobiographical film is also his strangest: warplanes, pelicans, parakeets with knives, and a grand-uncle maintaining a stack of blocks that is either the universe or a career.

In the wake of his mother's death and his father's remarriage, a headstrong boy ventures into a dreamlike world shared by the living and the dead in search of his missing stepmother.

metas.name: Whisper of the Heart
metas.description:
Captures a girl reverse-engineering a boy from the checkout cards in library books. Shizuku notices the same name borrowed every book before her, and the hunt becomes a film about deciding to make things — she writes a novel to find out if she can. The gentlest entry here, and the one about your exact activity: building skill into a position.

A love story between a girl who loves reading books and a boy who has previously checked out all of the library books she chooses.

metas.name: The Red Turtle
metas.description:
Captures a castaway's whole life on one island, without a word of dialogue. A man, a giant red turtle that keeps wrecking his rafts, and then a transformation the film simply places before you like weather. Ghibli co-produced; the water is drawn the way Parajanov drew cloth.

A man is shipwrecked on a deserted island and encounters a big red turtle, which changes his life.

metas.name: When the Wind Blows
metas.description:
Captures a retired couple preparing for nuclear war with government pamphlets and total faith in procedure. Hand-drawn, gentle, funny — Jim keeps saying the authorities know best while the fallout does its work. Raymond Briggs wrote it as a cartoon; it lands like a memorial.

A naive elderly British rural couple survive the initial onslaught of a nuclear war.

metas.name: World of Tomorrow
metas.description:
Captures a little girl visited by her own clone from 227 years later, who explains the future in a level, broken monotone. Seventeen minutes, stick figures, and the whole apparatus of memory-copying, failed immortality and inherited feeling. Your collection's shortest entries are 17 minutes; this is the other one that earns it.

A little girl is taken on a mind-bending tour of her distant future.

metas.name: Soul
metas.description:
Captures a jazz pianist who dies on the day of his break and has to argue his way out of the afterlife's intake office. The Great Before assigns personalities like case files; Joe's file keeps insisting the meaning was in the ordinary takes. Pixar's most explicit film about what a life is for, hidden inside its most musical one.

Joe is a middle-school band teacher whose life hasn't quite gone the way he expected. His true passion is jazz. But when he travels to another realm to help someone find their passion, he soon discovers what it means to have soul.

metas.name: Lily and Jim
metas.description:
Captures a blind date narrated by both daters at once, in split-screen stick figures, each privately misreading the other in real time. Thirteen minutes, made when he was barely out of film school, and the dual-internal-monologue structure is already fully his.

A blind date ends in disaster.

metas.name: Billy's Balloon
metas.description:
Captures toddlers being attacked by their own balloons, for no reason, in a park, while the parents don't notice. Five minutes, student-film crude, and still the purest statement of his comic physics: the world is soft, round, and hostile.

A boy and his balloon.

metas.name: Rejected
metas.description:
Captures an animator's commissioned ad cartoons being rejected one by one as they — and he — visibly fall apart. It starts with a banana announcing "my spoon is too big" and ends with the paper universe collapsing, blood pooling in the margins. Oscar-nominated, quoted for a quarter century, and it still feels unstable.

In the spring of 1999, the Family Learning Channel commissioned animator Don Hertzfeldt to produce promotional segments for their network. The cartoons were completed in five weeks. The Family Learning Channel rejected all of them upon review, and they were never aired...

metas.name: The Meaning of Life
metas.description:
Captures all of evolution and human history as a twelve-minute time-lapse that refuses to land on us. Creatures morph across geological time, crowds become patterns, patterns become individuals again; the title is the dare, and the ending is the shrug the title earns.

A sprawling look at the evolution of humankind, over the course of a billion years.

metas.name: Everything Will Be OK
metas.description:
Captures Bill, an ordinary man whose days — window light, a cough, a strange feeling in the street — start arriving out of order as an unnamed illness takes his memory apart. Part one of the trilogy; alone, it's the sunniest of the three and the most quietly frightening.

A series of dark and troubling events forces Bill to reckon with the meaning of his life - or lack thereof.

metas.name: I Am So Proud of You
metas.description: Captures Bill's family history told as a hereditary weather system: a mother, a man split into two by a train, a cousin in a rocket, the same darkness handed down like furniture. Part two of the trilogy, and the one where his prose — because by now the narration is prose — peaks.

metas.name: Wisdom Teeth
metas.description:
Captures a man having a wisdom tooth pulled, and his friend asking to pull the stitches. Five minutes, one dental thread, escalating commitment to a single bad idea. The palate cleanser of the catalogue, placed here as programmed.

Nigel does his best to help with his friend's simple request.

metas.name: World of Tomorrow Episode Two: The Burden of Other People's Thoughts
metas.description:
Captures little Emily travelling into the mind of her older clone, where memories are stored as literal rooms other people have moved into. The sequel to your #469 goes inward instead of forward: identity as a house full of other people's furniture.

Emily is visited by a backup clone of herself from the even-more distant future, as they must venture into each other's psyches in order to restore the clone's deteriorating mind.

metas.name: World of Tomorrow Episode Three: The Absent Destinations of David Prime
metas.description:
Captures a time-travelling husband erased from his own timeline, sending instructions backward to a wife who no longer remembers him. The most intricate of the three episodes — a love story conducted entirely through messages left in the wrong years.

A hidden memory sends David across the far reaches of time and space to solve a deadly mystery involving his time-traveling future selves.

metas.name: Me
metas.description:
Captures a musical about a self absorbing everything it touches, in twenty-two nearly wordless minutes. His newest: a round character rolls through a hand-drawn world converting people, places and finally the film itself into more of himself. After thirty years of drawing other people's inner lives, this is the one about the ego as a closed system — a transducer with the output looped to the input.

A musical odyssey about generational trauma and the retreat of humanity into itself.

metas.name: Kiki's Delivery Service
metas.description:
Captures a thirteen-year-old witch founding a delivery business in a seaside town, and competence arriving in stages: first flights, first customers, a slump where the gift itself fails. Work as dignity, kindness of strangers as infrastructure.

Along with her black cat Jiji, Kiki settles in a seaside town and starts a high-flying delivery service. Here begins her magical encounter with independence and responsibility, making lifelong friends and finding her place in the ...

metas.name: My Neighbor Totoro
metas.description:
Captures childhood before it learns to be endangered: two sisters new to the countryside, a mother in hospital kept almost off-screen, and the forest spirits who treat worry as weather. The children's happiness here is not ignorance — it's a skill the film takes seriously.

When two girls move to the country to be near their ailing mother, they have adventures with the wondrous forest spirits who live nearby.

metas.name: The Iron Giant
metas.description:
Captures a boy teaching a fifty-foot weapon that it can choose what it is. Cold War Maine, a beatnik sculptor, a government man terrified of the unknown — and the Giant learning the word for what he refuses to be. Friendship between unequals where the smaller one does the moral teaching; “you are who you choose to be” earned, not printed.

A young boy befriends a giant robot from outer space that a paranoid government agent wants to destroy.

metas.name: The Painting
metas.description:
Captures a world stratified by how finished it is. Inside an abandoned canvas live the Allduns (fully painted), the Halfies and the Sketchies (barely drawn), ruled by the completed who insist the Painter intended the hierarchy. A mixed group escapes the frame's edge to find the Painter and ask. Animated allegory about caste and creation, painted in the styles it moves through — the film's form is its argument.

Three characters of different social classes escape their unfinished painting in search of the Painter, hoping he will complete it.

metas.name: Persepolis
metas.description:
Captures a girlhood unfolding against a revolution, drawn in stark black and white. Marji in Tehran: veils imposed, uncles disappearing, contraband Iron Maiden, exile to Vienna, return, depression, departure again. The flat graphic style does what live action couldn't — a child's-eye scale where a key to paradise and a punk cassette are the same size, because to her they were.

A precocious and outspoken Iranian girl grows up during the Islamic Revolution.
